competitors.name: Hyphen Solutions (BuildPro / SupplyPro)
competitors.what_they_do: Incumbent construction management and supply-chain platform for production homebuilders. Its site says it is 'behind 1-in-3 homes in America' and lists BuildPro and SupplyPro. I could not confirm from the page whether it does trade-partner schedule confirmation, SMS, Spanish or voice, and the page lists 'AI' as a new product category with no detail. Scheduling and trade-partner communication is its home turf, so it is the biggest incumbent risk for builders at the larger end of the 20-300 homes/yr range.
competitors.scale_or_funding: 126,720 users across 565 builders (per its site). Long-established and entrenched with large builders.

competitors.name: Procore (Daily Log Agent and 4 other AI agents)
competitors.what_they_do: The Daily Log Agent turns field photos, emails, video and voice recordings into completed daily logs. The other agents are Deep Search, Submittal Review, RFI and Contract Review. No WhatsApp, Spanish-specific, subcontractor-coordination or scheduling agent appeared on the page. Case studies are commercial GCs (Haskell, McCownGordon, and others). Voice-to-log is the closest incumbent feature to the idea's transcription layer, but it is not crew confirmation.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Public company and the market leader in construction management software.

competitors.name: Fieldwire (Hilti)
competitors.what_they_do: Field task management, scheduling, punch lists and inspections, with a Spanish-language site and an AI feature ('Field Intelligence'). Aimed at GCs, specialty contractors, owners and architects, so it is not spec-builder-specific. It is app-based, and I found nothing on WhatsApp or voice-note input.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Owned by Hilti; says it powers over 4,000,000 jobsites.

competitors.name: Trunk Tools (TrunkText)
competitors.what_they_do: AI for document-heavy GC workflows, including TrunkText, an SMS-based project Q&A tool. Customers are large GCs (Gilbane, Suffolk, Baker, Consigli). No voice, WhatsApp, Spanish or sub crew-coordination features appeared on the site.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Funding not stated on the page.

competitors.name: Rhumbix (Autodesk)
competitors.what_they_do: Mobile field workforce platform for timekeeping, production tracking and daily reports. It serves trade contractors and GCs, mostly commercial. The site shows no Spanish, voice or headcount-forecasting features.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Autodesk has signed an agreement to acquire it (announced on its homepage); says it serves over 1,000,000 projects.

competitors.name: Raken
competitors.what_they_do: Field-first daily reports, time tracking, production tracking and safety. It explicitly serves subcontractors and small-to-enterprise firms. I could not confirm Spanish, voice or AI from the page.

competitors.name: Assignar
competitors.what_they_do: Drag-and-drop crew and equipment scheduling with instant worker notification, aimed at civil, excavation, concrete, paving and rail contractors. It is the closest software analog to daily crew dispatch and confirmation, but it targets civil work, not residential spec builders.

competitors.name: JobTread and BuildTools (custom builder and remodeler PM)
competitors.what_they_do: Home builder and remodeler project management with scheduling, sub/vendor portals and daily logs; both have added AI features. JobTread charges about $5-20 per internal user per month, with free sub and vendor portal access. BuildTools (https://www.buildtools.com/) publishes read-only schedules to subs and mentions no SMS/mobile confirmation or Spanish support. Both are English, login-based portals. They set the price anchor for software in this segment, and either could add WhatsApp or voice as a feature.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Not shown on the pages. Both sell to custom builders and remodelers, and BuildTools customer quotes mention builders doing 8-12 projects a year.

white_space: Research coverage was thin. The WebSearch budget (200 of 200) was exhausted before my searches ran, so I had no search results at all. I did not use WebFetch as a search-engine workaround, and instead fetched about a dozen specific vendor and reference pages directly. Buildertrend returned 403 and NAHB's labor page returned 404. I did NOT check Crunchbase, YC, TechCrunch, Product Hunt or GitHub, so I could not confirm whether any startup already sells WhatsApp voice-note crew confirmation. On the pages I did fetch, no company combines all of the following: (1) WhatsApp voice notes as the only interface for foremen, with no app or login; (2) Spanish-first speech transcription of headcount and phase status; (3) a human bilingual coordinator who confirms next-day crews by 5 p.m. and calls backup crews; (4) a morning exception report to the builder; (5) per-house pricing aimed at 20-300 home/yr spec builders. Vendors on the market are either app-and-login tools (Procore, Fieldwire, Raken, JobTread, BuildTools), large-GC AI (Trunk Tools, Procore agents), civil crew dispatch (Assignar), or production-builder infrastructure (Hyphen). The unserved slice is the mid-size spec builder, where the foreman's phone and language is the system of record and the deliverable is a confirmed crew rather than software. It is unserved partly because it is a labor-arbitrage service business that VC-backed software companies avoid.
evidence_of_demand: Weak and mostly unverified. Three points support demand. (1) Builders pay for scheduling software at scale: Hyphen's site claims 565 builders and 126,720 users (https://info.hyphensolutions.com/), and JobTread prices at $5-20 per user per month (https://www.jobtread.com/). (2) AGC's newsroom headlines from August and September 2026 include 'Construction Workforce Shortages Remain Acute Despite Soft Market Conditions' (https://www.agc.org/newsroom), and NAHB's Eye on Housing cites 'worsening labor shortages' and 'lot and labor shortages' for single-family production (https://eyeonhousing.org/). Neither page had figures on immigration enforcement, so the ICE arrest numbers and the '15-20 houses stuck 6+ weeks' anecdote in the idea file are unverified. (3) Procore and Fieldwire (Spanish site) are investing in voice-to-log and multilingual features, which suggests the direction is validated but also that incumbents are moving toward it. I found no forum complaints, RFPs or evidence that anyone pays $300-500 per house per month for crew confirmation as a service. The price point is untested. It is far above software prices, so it can only be justified on the cost of idle days.
sharper_angle: Treat it as a managed service with the software hidden behind it, not as a software product, and recheck it once WebSearch budget is restored before committing. Sell 'crew confirmed by 5 p.m., or we call the backup' as an outcome, priced per house and tied to idle days avoided, for example a flat fee with a rebate or bonus per foundation, framing or concrete idle day saved. Go where the idle-day cost is highest (foundation, framing, concrete, roofing) in the Texas/Florida Spanish-speaking sub base. Do not compete with the builder's project management system: push the confirmed headcount and exception report into whatever they use (BuildPro, Buildertrend, JobTread or a spreadsheet) so the service is an add-on. That also blunts the Hyphen and Procore risk, since a builder on BuildPro can still buy this. Test a second buyer: framing and concrete subs with 10-30 crews who need to know which of their own crews showed up. Position the product as attendance forecasting and re-sequencing, and keep the immigration-enforcement framing out of sales materials (privacy by design: counts and progress only). Before building, run three manual pilots and get one builder to sign a per-house price of at least $300 to prove willingness to pay.
